c256.summary: Issue #256 (Lingikogu) is fully ruled and seeded on schema; nothing UI is built. Contract: an admin-managed, ordered list of named URLs, collective-level, members-read-only, no forward markers left open, one first-use scenario (Joosep's Crede recordings) explicitly ruled to need no extra authorization gate.

findings.topic: 1. Operative UI contract as of the LAST word
findings.fact: Collective-level 'link' list: admins can add, edit, reorder, and remove links; members (any rights-holder below _editor on the collective) can only read the list in a stable order. No event-level or season-level attachment — deliberately not designed for. One collection per collective, reachable presumably from the collective/admin area (no specific nav slot was named in any comment).
findings.evidence: Final scoping comment (Gama, 2026-09-09T15:30:55Z, 'Signed off as an app extension type. `ready`.'): 'Admins add and remove. Members read.' ... 'Placement: Collective-level. One collection per collective ... Event-level attachment is deliberately not designed for; it is a genuinely useful later thing and it does not solve today's ask.' Done-when checklist in same comment: 'A collective's links are listed in a stable order members can read.' / 'Admins can add, edit, reorder and remove; members cannot.' / 'A link with no description renders without an empty line where one would be.' / 'URLs are stored as given. No normalising, no scheme-guessing, no validation beyond non-empty.'

findings.topic: 2. Live schema facts — link type IDs, prop-defs, add_from, sharing
findings.fact: Type-def IDs: polyphony `6aa2398620ebf490c690ab23`, mvox_crede `6aa239d620ebf490c690ab64`. 4 prop-defs each: name (string, required), url (string, required), description (string/optional, one line), display_order (number, manual ordinal). add_from resolves to `database` (the collective root) on BOTH dbs — NOT `organization` (organization type was retired in #161, same correction #265 needed). Type-level and prop-def `_sharing` = `domain` (matches sibling `section`/`repertoire_item` type-defs), `_inheritrights: true` — this is empirically checked, not inherited from `database`'s own type-def sharing (which is `public`). Zero `link` instances created — pure structure only.
findings.evidence: Perotin, 2026-09-10T05:03:42Z ('Live provisioning complete — both databases'): 'polyphony: link type-def 6aa2398620ebf490c690ab23. mvox_crede: link type-def 6aa239d620ebf490c690ab64. 4 prop-defs each — name url description display_order — plus add_from: database. 6/6 steps, 0 failures on both dbs. Zero link instances created ... Independently re-verified two ways ... a direct read confirms _sharing: domain / _inheritrights: true on the type-def and all 4 prop-defs, both dbs — matching the definition in scripts/migrations/lib/mvox-schema-extensions.ts exactly. Parent resolves to the database type-def (the collective root) — organization was confirmed absent on both dbs before writing the definition ... the same correction admin_member_record needed on #265.' Also Perotin, 2026-09-09T22:02:43Z ('Premise correction at prep time'): 'Parent resolves to database (the collective root), not organization — the org type was retired in #161 ... Type-level sharing = domain, matching the live section/repertoire_item sibling type-defs on both dbs — checked empirically, not inherited from database's own type-def sharing (public); the same trap #265's toggle hit first.' Ledgers committed at `ae4568b`, verification comment 2026-09-10T05:07:39Z confirms 'mvox_crede: dryRun: false, linkTypeId 6aa239d620ebf490c690ab64 (matches), instancesCreated: 0, six steps all created.'

findings.topic: 3. In-scope vs deferred/out — forward markers
findings.fact: IN scope for this UI slice: admin list/add/edit/reorder/remove of links at collective level; members read-only. OUT/deferred (never designed for now): event-level or season-level link attachment (explicit future possibility, not scoped); members-can-add model (future change, not foreclosed but not this slice); date field or type-marker field on links (rejected as unneeded guesses). The one forward marker that was opened (whether creating real Joosep-archive link instances needs its own PO authorization, like a data-migration gate) was explicitly OPENED and then CLOSED by the same person (Gama) in the last comment.
findings.evidence:
Final comment, Gama, 2026-09-10T05:07:39Z, quoted in full: '## Closing my own forward marker, because leaving it open would cost more than it protects

I flagged that the first-use step — Joosep's recordings archive — creates real link instances on a database holding real people, and would need its own authorisation. On the UI slice as now scoped (admin list / add / edit / reorder / remove), that is wrong, and I would rather say so than let a warning sit there breeding ceremony.

The first use is an admin typing links into the app. That is a person using the product for its purpose, not a migration against a live database. It needs no authorisation from us, and asking for one would be inventing a gate around ordinary use.

The precedent is exact: #282. The schema half was ours; Mihkel delegated real-value entry to Joosep and the admins. Same split here — we provision the type, the people who own the content put the content in.

One condition would change this, and it is worth naming so nobody has to guess: if the archive arrives as a file to be loaded rather than links entered by hand, that is a bulk write against mvox_crede and takes its own gate, its own dry run and its own ledger — exactly like this seed did. Say so when the time comes and it stops being ordinary use.

(*PO:Gama*)' Event-level attachment deferred per the 2026-09-09T15:30:55Z comment: 'Event-level attachment is deliberately not designed for; it is a genuinely useful later thing and it does not solve today's ask.'

findings.topic: 4. First-use implication — Joosep's recordings archive / real data on crede
findings.fact: The archive (f.io/GCkGMr5J share) is context for the commission, not part of this slice's scope or acceptance criteria. Creating the actual link instance(s) on mvox_crede (a database holding real people/PII) is explicitly ruled to be ORDINARY PRODUCT USE by an admin, needing no PO/team-lead authorization gate — treated the same as any admin typing content into the live product, precedent-matched to #282 (schema half ours, real-value entry delegated to Joosep/admins). This only flips to needing its own gate if the archive arrives as a bulk file-load rather than hand-entered links.
findings.evidence: Quoted verbatim above (finding 3) from Gama, 2026-09-10T05:07:39Z: 'The first use is an admin typing links into the app. That is a person using the product for its purpose, not a migration against a live database. It needs no authorisation from us, and asking for one would be inventing a gate around ordinary use. The precedent is exact: #282.' Also the type's Done-when checklist item: 'A collective's links are listed in a stable order members can read' plus 'Zero link instances created (empty structure only, per commission — Joosep's Crede recordings archive is a separate follow-up once a surface exists)' (Perotin, 2026-09-10T05:03:42Z) — confirming the archive entry is a follow-up AFTER the UI slice ships, not a gate on shipping it.

findings.topic: 5. Open questions the comments leave unruled (decision points for args, not decided here)
findings.fact: Nothing about the entity type or its default policy is open — placement, properties, creators tier, and visibility are all explicitly stated as fully settled ('Nothing about the entity type is open', Gama 2026-09-05T10:05:33Z). The only items left genuinely open as FUTURE possibilities (not blocking this slice, and not to be decided by the pipeline args) are: (a) whether to later widen add/remove rights from admins-only to members-can-add — explicitly called a 'future change, not foreclosed'; (b) whether/how to later attach links at event level — explicitly 'a genuinely useful later thing', deliberately undesigned; (c) whether a future date or type-marker field gets added — explicitly deferred as unneeded guesses, additive if ever needed. No UI navigation slot (which page/tab hosts the admin list) is specified in any comment — that placement-within-the-app-nav decision is left to whoever scopes the UI slice.
findings.evidence: Gama, 2026-09-05T10:05:33Z: 'The shape is now fully settled — placement (organization-parented, collective-level), properties (name, url, description, display_order), creators tier, and visibility. Nothing about the entity type is open.' Gama, 2026-09-05T10:05:33Z on creators: 'A members-can-add collection remains open as a future change, not foreclosed.' Gama, 2026-09-09T15:30:55Z: 'Event-level attachment is deliberately not designed for; it is a genuinely useful later thing.' No comment names a specific nav location (tab name, route, menu entry) for the admin link-list surface.

findings.topic: 6. Rights/sharing posture of link entities
findings.fact: Ruled sharing posture: link entities inherit domain-tier sharing cascaded from the collective (org/database) at create time — visible to choir members, NOT to the public internet — explicitly confirmed by Mihkel as correct for a recordings archive, with an explicit caveat that this is not a privacy guarantee over the linked destination itself. Creation right: parent_right `_editor` (admin/owner tier on the collective) — ruled as the smaller, additive claim. Live-verified actual sharing value on both dbs is `domain` at the type-def and all 4 prop-defs, `_inheritrights: true`, and the parent resolves to `database` not `organization`.
findings.evidence: Mihkel ruling via Gama, 2026-09-05T10:05:33Z: '2. Members-only visibility confirmed. The _sharing cascade from the domain-tier organization is right for a recordings archive. ... domain-tier sharing is not a privacy guarantee over the destination. It governs who sees the link inside mvox.' Same comment on creators: '1. Creators tier: admins only. parent_right _editor as sketched. My reasoning was accepted — it is the smaller claim, and widening later is additive whereas narrowing later takes something away from people already using it.' Live verification, Perotin 2026-09-10T05:03:42Z: 'a direct read confirms _sharing: domain / _inheritrights: true on the type-def and all 4 prop-defs, both dbs ... Parent resolves to the database type-def (the collective root) — organization was confirmed absent on both dbs.'

No route/page hosts a collective-root list+reorder surface today the way roster hosts sections (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte) — link would need a new host, but the data-module template is sectionActions.ts.

Read src/lib/repertoire/repertoireData.ts (193 lines, listRepertoireItems 48-78) and repertoireActions.ts function offsets via grep (all match prior research's cited line numbers exactly). findings.topic: 2. Navigation
findings.fact: NAV_ENTRIES lives in src/lib/nav/entries.ts (74 lines total) — still a fixed 6-item array (agenda/roster/profile/library/admin/collectives), each entry {key, label: ()=>m.nav_x(), route, icon, visible(ctx)}. No links row, no reserved gating slot. A new entry needs: an i18n key `nav_<name>` added to all 4 messages/*.json (en/et/lv/uk, verified all 4 currently in sync with 6 nav_ keys each), a new array entry with a `visible` predicate, and (since link is admin-edit/member-read, not admin-only) `visible: () => true` like agenda/roster/profile/library — NOT the `ctx.isAdmin`-gated pattern used by the admin entry, since members must be able to read the list even though only admins can mutate it.

findings.topic: 4. Entu data-access layer
findings.fact: Pattern unchanged: pure client-side SPA (ssr=false in src/routes/+layout.ts, JWT from localStorage, no server load functions anywhere — grep for +page.ts/+layout.ts under routes finds only the root +layout.ts). entuFetch(db, path, token, opts, fetchImpl) in src/lib/entu/request.ts is the sole wire layer (db is a URL path segment, not a constant — multi-collective). resolveTypeId (src/lib/seasons/entuSeasons.ts:26-50) resolves `_type` to a cached reference id via `entity?_type.string=entity&name.string=<typeName>`, used at create time as `{ type: '_type', reference: typeId }` — never a string. Search uses `_type.string=<name>&_parent.reference=<id>`. sectionActions.ts (or repertoireActions.ts) is the copy-template: sectionActions.ts is the closer template per finding 1.
findings.evidence: Read src/lib/entu/request.ts header comments (SPA/no-BFF architecture note) and src/lib/seasons/entuSeasons.ts:26-50 (resolveTypeId). findings.topic: 5. Standing-rule surfaces + rights gating idiom post-313
findings.fact: adminStore.ts (src/lib/nav/adminStore.ts, 159 lines) is the current rights idiom for database-entity-level (collective-level) rights: readDbRightsLists (48-96) reads `_owner`/`_editor` off the DATABASE entity by id; resolveAdmin (98-113) returns AdminState ('loading'|'admin'|'not-admin'|'error'); resolveOwnerTier (137-152) returns OwnerTier ('owner'|'editor'|'none'|'error'). This is the right idiom for a link surface, not repertoire's per-season manageRightsFrom — the schema commit (mvox-schema-extensions.ts:427) sets link's creator right to `parent_right _editor` on the `database` entity, i.e. exactly what adminStore/resolveOwnerTier already resolves. Testid convention confirmed unchanged: kebab-case, entity-noun-prefixed (`work-*` on repertoire, `section-*`/`roster-section-*` on roster) — a link surface would likely use `link-*`. i18n: flat Paraglide messages, 4 locales (en/et/lv/uk) all currently in sync, no existing `link_*`/`lingikogu_*` keys. Native-controls rule not specifically re-probed this turn but no new custom-widget code exists for link (nothing built yet) so nothing to check.
findings.evidence: Read src/lib/nav/adminStore.ts in full. Grepped data-testid in RepertoireElement.svelte and roster/+page.svelte. Grepped nav_ keys across messages/*.json.

findings.topic: 1. Operative contract (verbatim, last comment on #277, 'ready')
findings.fact: Build: 'A per-season entry point, not a picker. Each upcoming season the admin may manage gets its own way in; choosing from the season you are looking at beats a dropdown duplicating the list beside it.' Explicitly rejected: a season picker/dropdown, and 'make creation set the manageable season' (called out in the earlier comment as trading a dead end for a hidden mode). Done-when: (1) admin can open the management panel for ANY upcoming season they hold rights on, not just the soonest; (2) the panel states which season it is managing, visibly, whenever more than one is manageable; (3) switching the managed season leaves no stale state from the previous one — repertoire, series rows, in-flight writes belong to the season that is open ('manageableSeasonId changing is a context switch and behaves like one'); (4) rights are re-derived per season — manageableSeasonRights not carried across a switch; (5) existing behaviour byte-identical when only one season is manageable, no new control appears for the common case. 'Watch for': criteria 3/4 are flagged as the likely break point, explicitly compared to the collective-switch shape that produced #287/#296/#297/#299, with an explicit instruction to reuse the existing generation-guard idiom rather than invent a season-scoped variant.

findings.topic: MECHANICAL #256 — zero existing type-name references, but a naming decoy
findings.fact: No src/ file references the `link` entity type today (grep for 'mvox_link', 'link_type' etc. is empty) — this is a greenfield surface. BUT the bare string 'link' is heavily overloaded already by the unrelated account-linking OAuth feature (`intent: 'link'` throughout src/lib/auth/state.ts, src/routes/auth/[provider]/build-oauth-init-url.ts, src/routes/auth/callback/run-callback-exchange.ts, src/routes/profile/+page.svelte). Any grep-based blast check for the new type during implementation must filter these out; a careless `grep link` will drown the real hits.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "'link'" src/ returned ~20 hits, all `intent: 'link'` OAuth-linking sites; zero hits for the entity type itself.

findings.topic: MECHANICAL #256 — the schema shape now live
findings.fact: Type `link` is provisioned (empty, 0 instances) on both polyphony and mvox_crede: parent = `database` (collective root, post-#161; NOT `organization`), `_sharing: domain`, `inheritsRights: true`, creators `parent_right _editor` (admins add/edit/reorder/remove; members read-only), props `name` (string, required), `url` (string, required, stored verbatim — no validation/normalising per explicit ruling), `description` (string, optional), `display_order` (number, optional, mirrors `section`/`repertoire_item`). No creator/author property — links don't record who added them, so the invite-created-vs-auto-provisioned-person axis is not relevant to #256.

findings.topic: MECHANICAL #256 — nav-count specs WILL break on a new nav entry
findings.fact: `src/lib/nav/entries.ts` exports `NAV_ENTRIES` (currently 6: agenda, roster, profile, library, admin, collectives) — this is the exact insertion point for a `links` nav tab. `src/routes/page.navshell-merge.spec.ts` hardcodes the count TWICE: `expect(NAV_ENTRIES.map(e=>e.key)).toHaveLength(6)` (line 271) and `expect(navAnchors(container)).toHaveLength(6)` (line 292). Both will fail the moment a 7th entry is added and must be bumped to 7 as part of the #256-UI slice. `NavShell.spec.ts`'s own length assertions (lines 406/415/442/471/491) use a local `testEntries` fixture, not real `NAV_ENTRIES` — unaffected.

findings.topic: AXES — the reusable generation-guard idiom for #277 lives IN-FILE, not in the extracted roster module
findings.fact: Two distinct generation-guard idioms exist at HEAD: (1) an extracted `createRouteLoadMachine` in src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts (generation counter + `isCurrent(g)` getter), used only by src/routes/roster/+page.svelte for collective-switch guarding (the #287/#296/#297/#299 lineage Gama's ruling cites). (2) A bespoke, already-present `requestId`/`thisRequest` counter directly in src/routes/+page.svelte (declared line 705, bumped `++requestId` at line 795, checked at ~10 sites through line 1075+), PLUS two sibling per-read tickets `worksLoadId` and `scheduleLoadId` (lines 723-729) added for finer-grained races within one load — an established in-file precedent of 'add a new counter for a new independent race' rather than overloading one. Critically, `requestId` today bumps ONLY on a collective switch, never on a season switch, because only one season has ever been manageable. #277 introduces a genuinely new invalidation trigger (picking a different manageable season) that neither existing counter currently covers — the direct, minimal-footprint reuse is to extend/mirror the in-file `requestId`-sibling pattern (a new ticket bumped when `manageableSeasonId` changes) rather than importing the roster page's `routeLoad.ts` machine into +page.svelte.
findings.evidence: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:149 (createRouteLoadMachine) + src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts:77-137; src/routes/+page.svelte:701-729 (requestId/worksLoadId/scheduleLoadId doc comments and declarations).

findings.topic: AXES — rights-tier idiom for both slices is settled and reusable

Directly applicable to #256 (admin-only add/edit/reorder/remove) and to #277's new per-season entry point (visible only where the viewer holds editor rights on that season).
